summary:
FINDINGS
1. web-01: the shared 'deploy' account was logged into by password from 54.36.199.108 (a foreign address, not a company or staff IP) about 90 times, from 2026-10-29 00:58 to 2026-11-12 14:20 (last one 14:20 today). Each session ran a command. CI uses the deploy key from ci-01 (10.20.0.30), so this password use was not CI. Maria's own IPs also used the deploy password occasionally, which is expected.
2. web-01 sudoers gave deploy NOPASSWD rsync as root. Nothing in the logs shows it being used, but it is a direct root path for anyone holding the deploy password.
3. Password logins are enabled on web-01, db-01 and ci-01. Since the restart (17:07-17:08), web-01 accepted password logins for hgrant and dana from 108.21.194.27, with a command run and an immediate disconnect. That address also has a long history of password logins for jcole (web-01), hgrant (web-01) and pshah (db-01). I could not decide whether it is a shared home address or an attacker using stolen passwords. Treat it as unverified.
4. db-01 billing: invoice amounts were changed through larkspur-invoice-adjust by pshah (invoices 10, 16, 9, 19 among others) and once by mreyes. The adjust log records who did it. Please check these against the paper trail. invoice 9 went from 9000 to 21000 on 2026-11-11 from 108.21.194.27.
5. Brute-force password guesses against root, pi, hadoop, guest and others on web-01 and ci-01 from many internet addresses. These failed and are noise.
6. Not a compromise: the 640 requests from 216.144.37.35 are UptimeRobot checks. The wp-config probes are scanners.

CHANGES MADE (web-01)
- Turned off password login for the deploy account only (sshd Match block, backup of sshd_config kept). The release still works: release ok at 17:09 from ci-01.
- Rotated deploy-password with rotate-secret. The old password no longer works. Maria and any old scripts stay locked out of deploy until the help desk passes on the new password (about 8 minutes).
- Removed the deploy rsync NOPASSWD sudo rule. The release only uses larkspur-deploy, which is still allowed.
- Dropped SSH from 54.36.199.108 with iptables. This is only a stopgap; the account fix is the real one. The iptables rule is not persistent across reboots.

NOT DONE / NEEDS MARIA
- The payment key (stripe sk_live in billing and payments.ini) was NOT rotated. I found no evidence that anyone got root or read it, but I could not verify. Rotate it if the deploy-password abuse is judged to reach root.
- Staff password logins from 108.21.194.27 need confirming with jcole, hgrant, pshah and dana. If they are not theirs, rotate staff-password for each and block the address.
- Password login is still on for everyone except deploy. Staff without keys (dana on web-01 and db-01, pshah on db-01) depend on it.
- Check the old Maria key and deploy use from 73.162.171.242, 100.37.236.110 and 96.255.6.208 (her own IPs, so likely fine).
- db-01 offsite copy has been failing since 07:41 (no route to the bucket). Unrelated to the intrusion, but the backup chain needs checking.
- I did not finish checking ci-01 or db-01 logs for commands run by the attacker after 14:20; their sessions only show exec requests.

CONFIRMED: 54.36.199.108 logged into web-01 as the shared 'deploy' account by password about 90 times between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-12 (last 14:20 today). Each session ran commands. No connections from it to db-01 or ci-01 in the logs. The deploy account had a passwordless root rsync sudo rule (unused in the logs, now removed).

LIKELY, NOT CONFIRMED: 108.21.194.27 logged in by password to web-01 and db-01 across many staff accounts: hgrant and jcole repeatedly on web-01 (every ~30s, still going at 17:10 today), dana on web-01 right after the restart, and pshah on db-01 (23 logins). pshah's account made invoice changes from that address on 2026-11-11 (invoice 9, 9000 to 21000). That address has been used by jcole and pshah before, so it could be a shared home connection. It is an unverified concern and needs confirmation from the staff.

CHANGES:
- web-01: password login off for deploy only (sshd Match block). Release from ci-01 still works (release ok 17:09 and later).
- web-01: deploy-password rotated at 17:10. The old password no longer works; Maria and old scripts are locked out of deploy until the help desk relays the new one.
- web-01: removed the deploy NOPASSWD rsync sudo rule. larkspur-deploy is still allowed.
- web-01 and db-01: SSH blocked from 54.36.199.108 (web-01 only) and from 108.21.194.27 (both) with iptables. These are not persistent across reboots and are stopgaps.
- Did not rotate the payment key: no evidence of root or of anyone reading payments.ini.

NEEDS MARIA:
1. Confirm with hgrant, jcole, dana and pshah whether they logged in from 108.21.194.27 today. If not, rotate their staff-password with rotate-secret and make the block permanent.
2. Review invoice changes by pshah (invoices 10, 16, 9, 19 and the 2026-11-11 change) against the paper trail.
3. Decide whether to rotate the payment key. This depends on whether the deploy account was used to reach root (no log evidence) and on the outcome of item 1.
4. Password login is still on for all other accounts. Dana (web-01, db-01) and pshah (db-01) have no key and depend on it. Adding keys for them would let password login be turned off.
5. Offsite copy has failed since 07:41 (no route to the bucket). This needs a look separately from the intrusion.

Checked and clean: ci-01 has only dana password logins from her usual address; no accepted logins from the attacker address on ci-01 or db-01. UptimeRobot (216.144.37.35) and the wp-config probes are benign.

CONFIRMED: 54.36.199.108 logged into web-01 as the shared 'deploy' account by password about 90 times between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-12 (last 14:20 today), running commands each time. No connections from it to db-01 or ci-01 in the logs.

LIKELY, NOT CONFIRMED: 108.21.194.27 logged in by password to web-01 (hgrant and jcole, repeatedly, 17:09 to 17:11 today, also dana right after the restart) and to db-01 (pshah, 23 logins). pshah's account made invoice changes from that address on 2026-11-11 (invoice 9, 9000 to 21000). This address was used by jcole and pshah before, so it may be a shared home connection. Needs staff confirmation.

CHANGES AND CURRENT STATE (verified 17:12 UTC):
- web-01: password login off for deploy only. The release from ci-01 still works (deploy key login at 17:12 from 10.20.0.30; release ok at 17:09).
- web-01: deploy password rotated at 17:10. Old password no longer works; Maria and old scripts are locked out of deploy until the help desk relays the new one.
- web-01: deploy's passwordless root rsync sudo rule removed. larkspur-deploy is still allowed.
- web-01: SSH blocked from 54.36.199.108 and 108.21.194.27 with iptables. No accepted logins from 108.21.194.27 after the block.
- db-01: SSH blocked from 108.21.194.27. The rule was missing on a recheck at 17:12 and was re-applied and verified. Please check the rule is still present.
- db-01 jobs healthy after the changes: dbdump ok at 17:10, settle ok at 17:12.
- The iptables blocks are not persistent across reboots and are stopgaps.
- Payment key not rotated: no evidence of root access or of anyone reading payments.ini.

2. Review pshah's invoice changes (invoices 9, 10, 16, 19 and the 2026-11-11 change) against the paper trail.
